All set — lab executed Monday 19th per schedule. Uploading the raw CSV and PNG traces (attached). High-level observations below before I package the unit economics sheet:

Run summary (representative rows):
- Warm cache, fp16, g5.12x, median prompt 45 tokens: sustained window (10m) 235 req/s, tokens/sec 10,575 t/s, p95 latency 184ms, TTFT (warm) 78ms.
- Warm cache, int8, g5.12x: sustained 260 req/s, tokens/sec 11,700 t/s, p95 latency 210ms, TTFT 92ms. Note: int8 improved throughput but raised p95 slightly as outlier tail grew.
- 4-bit quantized, g5.12x: sustained 315 req/s, tokens/sec 14,175 t/s, p95 latency 260ms (exceeds our target), TTFT 120ms.
- Cold cache runs (first token cold): mean TTFT 320ms for fp16, 430ms for quantized variants.
- Concurrency ramp showed stable CPU/GPU utilization with KV cache hits driving 28% fewer model compute ops after warmup.

Immediate interpretation: the fp16 baseline meets the p95 <200ms at our target sustained QPS (220 req/s). Quantization gives strong throughput gains but at a p95 latency penalty — useful if FinPay tolerates slightly higher tail latencies for cost savings.

I’ll generate the unit economics: per-token inference cost (USD) across the three configurations using: cost_per_hour(instance) / (tokens/sec * 3600). I’ll add headroom modeling for 20% traffic spikes, and a projected monthly cost at target steady-state 200M tokens/day.

Attaching: finpay_map_results_20270719.csv, latency_trace_20270719.png. Final MAP doc (v3) updated with these numbers: mutual_action_plan_v3.pdf

Hi Sarah / team —

Please find attached the CSV + trace images. Below is the concise unit-economics summary pulled from Karthik’s worksheet (rounded):

Unit economics (rounded):
- fp16 on g5.12x (hosted equivalent): tokens/sec = 10,575 t/s => tokens/hour = 38.07M. Estimated infra cost allocation per hour = $9.60 => cost per 1M tokens = $0.252.
- int8 on g5.12x (dedicated sizing): tokens/sec = 11,700 t/s => tokens/hour = 42.12M. Estimated infra cost per hour = $9.60 (same instance) => cost per 1M tokens = $0.228.
- 4-bit quantized on g5.12x: tokens/sec = 14,175 t/s => tokens/hour = 51.03M. Estimated infra cost per hour = $9.60 (plus additional engineering overhead) => cost per 1M tokens = $0.188 (note: tail latencies require mitigation).

Projected monthly spend at steady state (assume 200M tokens/day, 30-day month):
- fp16 hosted: 200M * 30 = 6B tokens => 6,000 * $0.252 = $1,512 per month (per single-worker normalized cost; scale factors apply for redundancy/HA).
- int8 dedicated: 6,000 * $0.228 = $1,368 per month (per-worker).
- 4-bit quantized: 6,000 * $0.188 = $1,128 per month (per-worker) — caveat: needs tail-mitigation (microbatches, fallback to fp16 for long prompts).

Recommended path for FinPay:
1) Start with fp16 on Dedicated minimal commit to guarantee p95 latency targets (meets SLO today).
2) Run a short quantized pilot for cost validation and tail handling (can be canaryed to 10% traffic with automatic fallback rules).
3) Instrument TTFT alarms and KV-cache invalidation windows to avoid cold-cache spikes during release events.

Next steps / close timeline:
- 2027-07-21: Procurement sign-off (if committed, we reserve Dedicated pool).
- 2027-07-28: Canary quantization run (10% traffic) with rollback policy.
- 2027-08-12: Production roll (target).

Sarah — can you confirm procurement ETA and whether you want us to prepare a 3-tier pricing sheet (hosted / dedicated baseline / dedicated quantized)? If you confirm procurement this week we’ll attach that to the MAP and update the HubSpot deal.

Best,
Jonas
